content.title: About
content.content: Passion fruit (Passiflora edulis) is the fruit of a tropical vine, native to South America. The fruits are round or oval, with a tough purple or yellow rind that wrinkles as it ripens. Inside is aromatic, jelly-like pulp with crunchy edible seeds, tart and sweet in flavor. Passion fruit is eaten fresh and added to desserts, juices, sauces, and cocktails.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name passion fruit comes from the word passion: missionaries saw the flower as a symbol of the Passion of Christ.
There are purple and yellow passion fruits.
The fruit is considered ripe when its rind becomes wrinkled.
Brazil is one of the largest producers of passion fruit.
Passion fruit seeds are edible and crunchy.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion and helps you feel full.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and skin.

items.title: Contains carotenoids
items.content: The body partly converts carotenoids into vitamin A.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Contains polyphenols
items.content: The polyphenols in passion fruit have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Passion fruit can cause allergic reactions, including in people with latex allergy.

items.title: Rind and unripe fruit
items.content: The rind and unripe fruit contain cyanogenic compounds, so the rind is not eaten and it is better to choose ripe fruit.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Passion fruit is acidic and may cause heartburn or irritate tooth enamel.

items.title: Sugar in juices and desserts
items.content: Ready-made passion fruit juices, syrups, and desserts often contain a lot of added sugar.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cut a ripe passion fruit in half and eat the pulp with a spoon, seeds included. Add the pulp to yogurt, smoothies, desserts, sauces, and cocktails; the juice can be strained to remove the seeds. Do not eat the rind.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Leave firm fruit at room temperature to ripen. Store ripe fruit in the refrigerator for one to two weeks. The pulp can be frozen.
